content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 7.2 (p0026) was the only MFN provision in the agreement, and it ran against us — an open-ended duty to disclose and match, for Vendor's benefit, any more favourable third-party offer before engaging another provider. No defined product, no 12-month limit, no like-for-like carve-outs, so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory. It also contradicted Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists, so nothing in our favour was touched.

**Cure (preferred level, single surgical replace):** the obligation in 7.2 is converted into an express statement that Customer has no duty to disclose or match any competing offer, with the fallback (single defined product, 12 months, like-for-like carve-outs) offered in the comment.
